 India will start the five-match T20I series against New Zealand with the first T20I from Thursday onwards. The assignment will be a crucial one for Shreyas Iyer.

 Shreyas Iyer vs Suryakumar Yadav T20I captaincy comparison (BCCI/ICC Photos) 
 Shreyas Iyer as captain has enjoyed a stellar run in the IPL but the 31-year-old has struggled to replicate it for India in T20Is. Since taking up the role earlier this year, Iyer-led India have faced some humiliating defeats, including a whitewash against Ireland. Even the last assignment before traveling to New Zealand, which was a five-match T20I series against West Indies at home, ended in 2-2 stalemate. In between there has also been losses against England and barring the gold medal at Asian Games there has been very little to celebrate.
 This has often led to comparison with his predecessor Suryakumar Yadav, who was unceremoniously dropped from the side after leading India to T20 World Cup triumph at home.
 Former India assistant coach Abhishek Nayar recently weighed-in on the subject and said the comparison is "out of the way", given how much Iyer has played away from India already. He also said that winning in New Zealand will earn Iyer respect of everyone around him.
 Also Read | Partnership that keeps delivering: Kumar Sangakkara and Mahela Jayawardene’s success beyond the pitch 
 India will start the five-match T20I series against New Zealand with the first T20I from Thursday onwards. The assignment will be a crucial one for Iyer, who lost series to Ireland and England right at the start of his T20I captaincy stint and could not win a match in either of them. If the New Zealand series follows the script that unfolded in the UK earlier this year, pressure will only mount on Iyer, who is expected to lead India in the T20 World Cup to be held in Australia and New Zealand in two years' time.

 Speaking on JioHotstar's 'Out or Not Out' show, Nayar pointed out how much India played at home under Suryakumar, leading to the T20 World Cup, while Iyer has mostly been engaged in away assignments. "It is not about whether he is worthy or not in comparison to Surya, because, at that time, India played a lot of series in India. They did not travel a lot. After Shreyas Iyer took up captaincy, they have gone to England, and now they are going to New Zealand. So, a lot of the T20Is have been played away from home, in Zimbabwe and Japan," he said.
 "I remember that, building up to the T20 World Cup, we were playing a lot more at home and in subcontinental conditions than away. So, that comparison is out of the way. Whenever you go to New Zealand and win in foreign conditions, I think that captain will feel in control of the team and earn the respect of everyone around him, because that's where you are judged the most. So, if you win, like they say, it is a star on your chest, going to New Zealand and winning the series. It did not happen in England, but if it does happen here, it will be one of those things for him personally, that 'I can win abroad as well' as a captain," he added.
 What do the numbers tell 
 Iyer has so far won 11, lost eight in 21 T20Is as captain. Two matches have ended in no result, making his win percentage just over 52. Six of these losses have come in overseas conditions, with two coming against West Indies at home recently. As a skipper, Iyer has lost the series in Ireland, England and drawn against West Indies at home. But he has also won the Asian Games gold, against Zimbabwe away from home and against Afghanistan at home too.
 With 40 wins in 52 matches, just eight losses, two ties and no results each, Suryakumar, with a win percentage of 76.92, is among the most successful T20 leaders ever in the history of sport.
